title: Bacterial Immobilization for Imaging by Atomic Force Microscopy
protocol: Cut the mica with scissors to fit the AFM microscope (approx. 22 × 30 mm).
Cleave the mica on both sides using tape until only smooth unbroken layers remain.
Add 100 ml of distilled water to a laboratory bottle.
Heat the bottle in a microwave until the water begins to boil.
Weigh out 0.5 grams of gelatin and add it to the hot distilled water.
Gently swirl the bottle until the gelatin is completely dissolved.
Cool the gelatin solution to 60-70 °C.
Pour approximately 15 mL of the gelatin solution into a small beaker (20 mL).
Submerge the mica squares into the warmed gelatin solution and withdraw quickly.
Support the coated mica immediately, on edge, on a paper towel to dry in ambient air.
Reheat the excess gelatin solution to between 60-70 °C for reuse.
Pellet 1 mL of bacterial culture at 800 to 4,500 rcf.
Wash the pellet in the same volume of filtered deionized water or buffer.
Collect the cells again by centrifugation.
Resuspend the pellet promptly in 500 μL of nanopure deionized water or buffer.
Apply 10-20 μL of cell suspension to the gelatin-coated mica using a pipette tip without touching the surface.
Allow the surface to rest for 10 minutes.
Rinse the surface with a stream of water or buffer.
Place gelatin at a temperature of 60-70°C in a 20 ml beaker.
Immerse freshly cleaved mica squares into the gelatin using tweezers.
Withdraw mica squares and place them upright on a paper towel leaning against a micro centrifuge rack.
Place a droplet of bacterial sample on the mica and spread it with a pipet tip in both X and Y directions.
Allow the bacterial sample to incubate on the mica surface for at least 10 minutes.
Rinse the bacterial sample with distilled water.
Check for an opaque spot on the mica, indicating successful immobilization of bacteria.
